title: A Terminal for the Vector
premise: Elodie Coldharbour has spent a decade hauling cargo through contested orbits aboard the Vector, hiding the illegal memory-backups of her dead crewmates in the hold and her feelings for engineer Sefa Kwan behind protocol. When the research vessel Meridian returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children, carrying a message that could end the war between Earth's last two orbital states, Elodie is blackmailed into running it through the blockade. Along the way she must decide whether the backups in her hold are cargo, ghosts, or people — and whether delivering peace is worth surrendering the only home she has. In the end she broadcasts the message at the cost of the Vector itself, wakes the backups one final time to say goodbye, and chooses to stay with Sefa among the de-aged Meridian children rather than return to the life that kept her invisible.
about_author: Bram Yarrow is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who now writes science fiction from a houseboat on the North Sea coast. Their work explores how people stay human inside systems designed to make them interchangeable.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Elodie navigates the Vector through a contested shipping lane while quietly monitoring the hold where eleven illegal memory-backups sleep in cold storage. POV: Elodie. Establishes her double life and the ache of keeping ghosts; ends with a distress ping from an impossible vector.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Back Young
chapters.summary: The Vector answers the distress call and finds the research vessel Meridian adrift, its crew of forty reduced to children under ten, memories intact but bodies decades wrong. POV: Sefa. Wonder curdles into dread as they realize whatever did this came from deep space — and something followed them back.

chapters.title: Manifest Irregularities
chapters.summary: A blockade inspector boards the Vector and nearly discovers the hold. Elodie lies for the first time in ten years, and Sefa covers for her without being asked. POV: Elodie. The beat is intimacy born of complicity — and the first hint that someone official already knows about the backups.

chapters.title: What the Children Remember
chapters.summary: Aboard the Meridian, child-crew member Dr. Ilsa Voss, still a scientist inside a seven-year-old body, explains the message they carry: proof that the war's founding atrocity was staged. POV: Ilsa. Grief and clarity; she asks Elodie to carry it through the blockade because the Vector is nobody's ship — invisible.

chapters.title: Terms of Carriage
chapters.summary: The blockade commander, Rear-Admiral Osei, offers Elodie amnesty for the backups if she surrenders the message instead of delivering it. POV: Osei. Cold pragmatism masking fear; he believes the truth will shatter what remains of Earth's cohesion. Elodie refuses — and becomes a fugitive.

chapters.title: Eleven Passengers
chapters.summary: Running dark, Elodie finally speaks aloud to the backups, playing their stored voices through the cabin as she plots a route. POV: Elodie. A tender, haunted chapter revealing each backup belonged to someone she failed to save; Sefa listens at the door and says nothing.

chapters.title: The Long Way Around
chapters.summary: Sefa proposes a suicidal slingshot through debris fields no warship will enter. The crew debates: deliver the message, sell it, or burn it. POV: Sefa. Loyalty crystallizes into love declared clumsily mid-crisis; Elodie can't answer yet.

chapters.title: Interdiction at Ceres Gate
chapters.summary: Osei's patrol catches them anyway. To save the crew, Elodie offers herself and the backups as bargaining chips, buying passage by promising the message will be heard publicly before any faction controls it. POV: Elodie. Duty versus survival made literal; she signs away her freedom.

chapters.title: Held
chapters.summary: Imprisoned on the blockade flagship, Elodie meets the other side: a defector from the inner state who confirms the atrocity was staged — and reveals Osei knows, and is stalling until Earth's transmission loop expires and the evidence dies unread. POV: the defector, Anselm. The stakes sharpen: this isn't about delivery, it's about time.

chapters.title: Breakout
chapters.summary: Sefa and the de-aged children of the Meridian stage an absurd, brilliant rescue using the kids' small size and adult knowledge. POV: Ilsa. Comedy braided with heartbreak — children doing soldier's work — ending with Ilsa taking a wound meant for Sefa.

chapters.title: The Cost of Cargo
chapters.summary: Fleeing, they must jettison mass. The backups' pods are the heaviest thing aboard. POV: Elodie. The central choice arrives early: she refuses to dump the dead, and instead vents her own quarters, her history, everything personal she owns. Belonging redefined as what you refuse to lose.

chapters.title: Quiet Between Burns
chapters.summary: A breath of calm. Elodie and Sefa share a watch, and she finally answers his declaration — not with words but by giving him the key to the hold. POV: alternating brief sections. The love story lands softly against the ticking clock of Earth's transmission loop.

chapters.title: Osei's War
chapters.summary: Osei, exposed by Anselm's defection, doubles down: he'll destroy the Vector and blame the enemy state, unifying Earth in grief. POV: Osei. Tragic antagonist chapter — we see the logic of his lie and almost sympathize before he orders the kill.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Graveyard
chapters.summary: A full-burn pursuit through a battlefield littered with hulks from the war's first battle. Elodie flies like she never has, using the wrecks as cover. POV: Sefa. Adrenaline and awe; the Vector takes fatal damage to the drive.

chapters.title: One Burn Left
chapters.summary: Engineering assessment: enough thrust for the relay station or for escape — not both. The crew votes. Every hand goes up for the relay. POV: Sefa. The theme of price made communal; even the children vote yes.

chapters.title: Waking the Dead
chapters.summary: To run the damaged relay manually requires minds that know obsolete protocols — the backups' era. Elodie boots all eleven, temporarily, knowing they'll degrade within hours. POV: Elodie. Joy and devastation entwined: she gets one conversation with everyone she lost.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax part one: the awakened backups and the child crew seize the relay station under fire. Ilsa, dying or close to it, delivers the testimony in her own voice across every open channel. POV: Ilsa. Triumph shot through with loss as the truth floods the loop before it expires.

chapters.title: Osei's Choice
chapters.summary: With the message public, Osei's fleet hesitates. Confronted by Elodie on open comms — and by his own conscience — he stands down rather than fire on children and ghosts, then turns himself in. POV: Osei. Redemption earned at the cost of everything he built.

chapters.title: Eleven Goodbyes
chapters.summary: The backups begin to fade as planned. One by one they thank Elodie, absolve her, and release her from guilt she's carried for ten years. POV: Elodie. The emotional climax: grief transformed into permission to live.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Contested Orbits
chapters.summary: Ceasefire spreads system-wide as the staged atrocity reshapes politics. The Vector is condemned as unseaworthy; the crew is offered new postings, new identities, new lives. POV: Sefa. Bittersweet disbanding — the found family scatters toward futures they chose.

chapters.title: A Terminal for the Vector
chapters.summary: Elodie decommissions the ship alone, walking its length one last time, leaving the empty hold open to the light. She files the flight plan under a name that isn't hers anymore. POV: Elodie. Elegy and release; the title's meaning lands — a terminal is both an ending and a place you arrive.

chapters.title: Departures
chapters.summary: Months later: Elodie and Sefa board a slow liner bound for the colony world where the Meridian children are being raised, Ilsa's legacy carried forward. Elodie, once invisible, is recognized by a stranger who thanks her. POV: Elodie. Resolution: love chosen over duty survived, belonging finally accepted, the price paid acknowledged without regret.
